methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $15M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 2 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 13 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

methods.name: Public-Comp Anchoring

methods.rationale: Public Semiconductors P/S median is 20.4x across 3 tickers. Cannot apply without target's revenue.

data.narrative:
zeroRISC is a Seed-stage semiconductor company that has raised $15M to date. The Chips & Semiconductors sector encompasses a broad comp universe of 3 public companies (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers including Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, and SambaNova Systems, though a sufficiently tight peer set at the same stage and valuation tier is not available for direct median benchmarking.

The primary applicable valuation method is Stage-Progression, which applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-Series A advancement. Using the $15M total raised as a proxy for current valuation, this method implies a post-Seed valuation of $38M. Public Semiconductors comps (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) trade at a 20.4x Price-to-Sales median, but this approach cannot be applied absent disclosed revenue figures, which private companies rarely provide. The Peer-Median method is similarly not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum sample size thresholds.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $32M–$43M (centered on $38M) based on the single applicable triangulation method. The material uncertainty stems from the absence of revenue disclosure and insufficient narrow-stage peer data. Public comp anchoring would strengthen conviction if target revenue were available. Readers should treat this range as preliminary and expect meaningful revision upon revenue visibility or closer identification of comparable Seed-stage semiconductor companies.
